ac833b8b5e28.author: d1056283cf72
ac833b8b5e28.body:
Moving a WordPress site to a static stack is mostly about keeping what already works: the addresses people have bookmarked, the formatting editors spent years on, and the search rankings that took just as long. This post walks through the blocks a typical site uses and how they survive the move.

Columns and buttons

Before

Pages rendered by PHP on every request, a plugin for caching, another for images, and a theme that loads three versions of jQuery.

After

Plain HTML built once, one stylesheet, images sized at build time, and content edited in Contentrain Studio.

About the studio
Get in touch

The fastest request is the one the server never has to think about.

Every performance engineer, eventually

A table

  • Permalinks stay exactly where they were.
  • Categories, tags and authors keep their archives.
  • SEO titles and descriptions move with each post.

Tip: run the build locally before switching DNS, and compare the sitemap with the old one.

Links in a body follow the same rule: the about page by its old absolute address, the contact page by its WordPress short link, and what comes next, which is still a draft.
